_comment: The contract a decomposition tracker must satisfy. Authored by hand - this
is the one file under data/shared/ that is an input, not a build product.
It exists because a Smartsheet account reconfiguration on 2026-08-27
stripped every dropdown and formula from both trackers, and nothing in the
repo said what they should have been. Restoring them meant diffing two
sheets and guessing at intent. With this file, tools/validate_tracker.py
reports the drift and a future restore is mechanical.
'required' columns are the ones the generators read - a tracker missing one
cannot be built from. 'optional' columns are read when present and tolerated
when absent. Everything else on the sheet is meeting scratch space that this
repo neither reads nor commits.

Epic.note: Stable slug, the id every dependency resolves against.

Capability.note: capreq filename with 'capreq-' dropped. Renamed from 'Initiative' on 2026-08-18.

Baseline Priority.note: MoSCoW, pre-filled from the epic. Not edited in meetings.

2TS Required.note: Epic-level only. Child (story) rows leave this blank.

note: Direction is blocker -> dependent. An entry may carry a comma-separated
qualifier list and a marker: 'epic-x (Embedded, soft) [guess]'.
(hard) cannot start, (soft) cannot finish, untagged defaults to hard.
Never split this cell on commas naively. Stories can gate an epic too,
which is why it is Issues rather than Epics.

Jira Key.note: Most are  MCHTRNCS, however supporting teams may work under their own projects (e.g., Electronics epics are project ET).

note: Display only - drives the estimated indicator, never an edge or a count.
Roughly ordered by progress. 'Stories Created' came from the Embedded
tracker adopted 2026-08-28 and is the state after Estimated, once the
stories exist in Jira. Only 'Estimated' currently draws the indicator;
whether 'Stories Created' should also mark a node is an open question -
it is strictly further along, so arguably yes.
How firm the estimate is. Set in the evaluation meeting, not derived.
Medium when either applies:
- a decomposition or requirement update is needed but not yet detailed
(e.g. MCHTRNCS-197, MCHTRNCS-230)
- a develop or implement story is needed from Michael's team
Low when:
- a child story reads 'Gates Embedded-Core Work' and no Jira id has yet
been found to record as the blocker
High otherwise - the estimate stands on work already understood.

_comment: Keyed by SHEET NAME, which is what the API reports and what teams.py
records as sheet_name. A rename silently drops every check in a block
rather than failing one, so validate_tracker names a sheet it has no
block for, and load_live warns when the live name and the registry
disagree. Re-key both whenever a sheet is renamed - this sheet was
'DHayesScratch Embedded-Core Epic Decompositin' (typo included) until
'Epic Total (days)' was dropped from this contract on 2026-09-01. No
generator ever read it, effort is tracked in points rather than days,
and its presence or absence on any tracker is now immaterial to the
build. Do not re-add a check for it.
Nothing is checked on this sheet today. The block is kept, rather than
deleted, so validate_tracker does not report the sheet as unknown to
the contract - an empty block means 'no formula expectations', a
missing one means 'nobody has said'.
All three are CONDITIONAL COLUMN formulas keyed on JiraType, added
2026-09-01. A column formula normally applies one rule to every row,
which is why the epic/story split has to live inside the IF rather than
in which rows carry a formula - that is what makes a column formula
usable here at all, where a plain =SUM(CHILDREN()) could not be.
Story Points is DERIVED, never typed. On a story row it is
ROUNDUP(Duration/2) - the exact inverse of the agreed points scale at
its canonical values (2d->1, 3d->2, 5d->3, 10d->5). On an epic row it
sums its children. The column is locked on the sheet, which is correct:
the meeting's input is Duration in days, not points.
Caution: an off-scale Duration yields an off-scale point value. 7d
gives 4, and 4 is deliberately not on the 1/2/3/5 scale. Durations are
worth keeping on 2/3/5/10 if the points are to mean anything.
'Epic Total (days)' was removed from the sheet. Its purpose was reallocated to
an epic's Duration. It is deliberately NOT checked
here - no generator reads it and its presence is immaterial to the
build. Do not re-add a check for it.
The captured input is DURATION IN DAYS, on story rows. Story Points are
derived from it by the tracker (see the formulas block) and rolled up to
the epic. Nobody types a point value and nobody types an epic total.
Story points are not days. The conversion below is non-linear - it is a
story-point scale, so doubling the points more than doubles the effort.
Confirmed with the tech team lead 2026-08-30.
4 points is deliberately absent: the scale is 1/2/3/5 and a 4 in a
tracker is an error to correct, not a value to interpolate.
ROUNDUP(Duration/2) inverts this table exactly at its canonical values,
which is why it is the right derivation and not an approximation:
A Duration off that set produces a point value off the scale - 7d gives
4 - so the scale is only meaningful while Durations stay on 2/3/5/10.
No generator reads any of this.
Trackers may carry child rows: one per story, indented under its epic.
The generators read epics only.
Optional and per-sheet. Embedded is hierarchical (187 stories under 46 of its 87 epics); Electronics is flat. Both are valid.
TWO INDEPENDENT NOTIONS OF 'is this an epic' now exist, and they must
agree. This repo uses row hierarchy: parentId on the live path, the Epic
slug pattern on the CSV path. The SHEET uses the JiraType column, which
every conditional column formula added 2026-09-01 keys on. A row whose
JiraType disagrees with its indentation produces a graph and a set of
sheet numbers that describe different things, with nothing to say so -
an epic row marked Story silently gets ROUNDUP(Duration/2) instead of a
roll-up, and a story row marked Epic sums children it does not have.
validate_tracker --live cross-checks the two.
Enforced two ways, because the two load paths see different things:
live  a row with a parentId is a child and is skipped outright. Exact
and structural - an Epic value typed into a story row cannot put
it in the graph.
csv   a Smartsheet CSV export carries no hierarchy, so the Epic id must
match the slug pattern. Prose in the Epic column is skipped and
named on stderr.
Columns that are epic-level only, blank on children:
Epic, Capability, Baseline Priority, 2TS Required,Blocking Issues, Eval Status
Columns meaningful on a child row:
Title, Story Points
Story Points is the only column carried on BOTH: hand-entered on each
story row, and summed from the children on the epic row above it.
